correctness.rationale: The first-force argument is exact: before the first force a black vertex in V_i has W-w_i white neighbors; after it clears the complement, precisely w_i whites remain in V_i, which are forceable iff w_i<=k. This proves the all-set criterion in both directions. Maximizing the two white capacities proves F_k=N-max_i(min(k,n_i-1)+min(k,N-n_i)). At minimum size, witness i is equivalent to w_i=a_i for maximizing i, so ordinary inclusion-exclusion gives the stated minimum-set count. A literal dynamics verifier agrees on 694,928 initial-set checks across all ordered positive multipartite profiles through order 9 for k<=4.

value.rationale: The object and invariant are standard and motivated: complete multipartite graphs are a canonical dense class, and k-forcing is a standard propagation generalization of zero forcing. The theorem is structural rather than a routine numeric recomputation: it characterizes every feasible initial set, gives a closed exact minimum for all part profiles, and counts all minimum sets while correcting overlaps between multiple maximizing witness parts. It properly contains known k=1 and r=2 regimes without claiming their already-covered content.
